text:
sasha: FYI - the FP8 kernel rollout on H100/L40S just surfaced a small but consistent regression on the codegen canary. runs vs FP16 baseline: perplexity +2.4, pass@1 -0.7% on the small sampling suite. digging in now. :thinking:

mike: can you paste the canary summary and which build id / runtime flags were used?

sasha: build=rev-2026.3.7-fp8kern, runtime flags: `enable_fp8_kernels=1`, `mixed_precision_policy=auto`. Canary on h100-prod-pool-1. eval-bot summary below:

eval-bot: ```
config: baseline(fp16) | fp8_h100 | fp8_l40s
perp:   22.8          23.3      23.1
pass@1: 31.2%         30.5%     30.6%
notes: fp8_h100 shows largest delta, l40s smaller but non-zero
```

jin: I glanced at kernel traces — there are vector-width differences between the H100 and L40S GEMM kernels when FP8 path is used. tiling changes the accumulation ordering and reduces some headwise dynamic range, which affects the quantization scale heuristics.

karen: so this is a deterministic numerical drift from different reduction order, not a bug in quantization math?

jin: looks like a combo: vector widening on H100 changes how accumulators saturate, and our auto-scale picks slightly different per-column scales. that shifts softmax logits by small eps, enough to nudge sampled tokens.

mike: are results reproducible with fixed rng seeds? if yes, it's numerical, not sampling noise.

sasha: repro'd across seeds and batches. ran 10 reruns, same ordering of degraded examples. not noisy.

zane: quick mitigation: enable compatibility shim that forces 32-wide accumulation semantics (vector_widening_compat=true) so kernels use the narrower accumulation tiling matching FP16 path. we use that in a couple of customers for quant-aware rollouts. want to try a canary flip?

infra-bot: deploy request queued: canary-toggle-2051234567 by sasha -> target: h100-canary-3, start=2051234576

eval-bot: quick canary results after toggle:
```
config: fp8_h100 (compat shim)
perp: 22.9
pass@1: 31.1%
notes: nearly back to baseline within noise (delta -0.1%)
```

sasha: that looks promising. shim cost is ~3% throughput reduction on H100 from narrower tiling. tradeoff seems acceptable for now until we tune scale heuristics.

karen: we should root-cause: either adjust per-column scale estimator to be invariant to reduction order or add a post-softmax rescale calibration. which is lower-risk?

jin: short-term: shim + add a micro-benchmark that compares per-head activation ranges under FP16 vs FP8 kernels across sequence lengths. long-term: change quantizer to use max-abs over a merged-reduction estimate (simulate kernel tiling) so scale choice is stable across devices.

mike: action items: 1) roll FP8 with vector_widening_compat on prod H100 canary (sasha) 2) add micro-bench suite for headwise activations (jin) 3) write an eval that fails the rollout if pass@1 drops >0.5% (karen) 4) track perf impact per-route and allow per-model overrides (zane).

sasha: creating PR for runtime flag default and an infra patch to expose per-model override. PR link: https://redwood.internal/p/r/2254 (will post when available).

zane: also recommend a quick AWQ/GPTQ compare on affected models — FP8 deltas might interact with AOQ-style per-channel quantizers differently. add to bakeoff matrix.

eval-bot: noted. added jobs: awq_gptq_comparative_2051234579 targeting models: codegen-small, assistant-7b. will report in thread. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks. low-severity outage avoided. please post patch and I'll schedule a postmortem-lite if the regression recurs. :thumbsup:
